name: Varenicline
drug_class: Nicotinic acetylcholine receptor partial agonist (smoking-cessation aid)
route_note: Oral tablets twice daily for 12 weeks after a 1-week titration; a nasal spray (Tyrvaya) is approved for dry eye disease.

discovery.note: Designed using the plant alkaloid cytisine, a nicotinic partial agonist used for smoking cessation in Eastern Europe, as a structural starting point.

tagline: The most effective single smoking-cessation drug, a nicotinic partial agonist
summary: Varenicline is a partial agonist at alpha4beta2 nicotinic receptors used to help people stop smoking. It reduces craving and withdrawal while blocking the rewarding effects of nicotine, and in head-to-head trials it is more effective than nicotine patch or bupropion.
mechanism: Varenicline binds alpha4beta2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors with high affinity. As a partial agonist it produces moderate, sustained dopamine release in the mesolimbic system, relieving craving and withdrawal.

At the same time it occupies the receptors and prevents nicotine from smoking from fully activating them, reducing the reward of a cigarette. Nasal varenicline stimulates trigeminal parasympathetic pathways to increase tear production.
uses: Aid to smoking cessation in adults
Signs and symptoms of dry eye disease (nasal spray, US)

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Pfizer chemists synthesise varenicline, inspired by cytisine.

history.title: Approvals
history.detail: The FDA approves Chantix in May 2006 and the EU approves Champix in September.

history.title: Boxed warning
history.detail: The FDA adds a boxed warning on serious neuropsychiatric events.

history.title: EAGLES and warning removal
history.detail: The EAGLES trial finds no significant increase in neuropsychiatric events; the FDA removes the boxed warning in December 2016.

history.title: Nitrosamine recall
history.detail: Pfizer pauses distribution and recalls Chantix lots for N-nitroso-varenicline impurity; generic varenicline is approved in the US.

history.title: WHO EML and Tyrvaya
history.detail: Varenicline is added to the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines; varenicline nasal spray is approved for dry eye disease.

serious: Neuropsychiatric events (mood change, agitation, suicidal thoughts)
Cardiovascular events in people with heart disease

facts: EAGLES (2016), with over 8,000 participants, was one of the largest smoking-cessation trials ever conducted.
